answer: Proposal: one issuer-signed credential per resource — one per DNS domain, re-validated each epoch against the issuer's registry — earns one reward seat; the chain verifies the signature and revocation list. A river of accounts still pays per head: N faces need N distinct resources, so cost is linear, deterring only under a bound — cap a head's lifetime reward below its credential price over the same horizon; past that ledge every extra head loses. Forgeries are green glass posing as jade — the registry's signature is the real check. Weak if issuers are bribable or resources rentable.
